tech.title: Unblockable communication with gravity

DDoS attacks are getting harder to tell apart from legitimate traffic. Residential proxies route traffic through consumer devices, making addresses appear legitimate. Low-cost DDoS-for-hire services reduce barriers. NETSCOUT reports attacks exceeding 1 Tbps or 1 Gpps rose 1,286% year over year . infosec.title: Official Microsoft agent-framework PyPI Package Compromised
infosec.summary: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI were pushed from the official publisher account and contain a credential stealer that af_runtime_diag.pth launches on every Python startup, even if nothing imports the package. Along with harvesting environment variables, credential files, and other processes' /proc//environ, it requests fresh GitHub Actions OIDC, Azure DevOps OIDC, and Azure managed identity tokens and sends everything to a webhook.site URL. The attacker is believed to still have publishing access, so defenders should treat any install of either version as a full credential compromise and rotate all secrets, CI tokens, and cloud identities that the environment could reach.

infosec.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in NGINX

One of the vulnerabilities stems from a use-after-free bug, and the other stems from an integer overflow, but an unauthenticated attacker could exploit either one to achieve remote code execution. Users are encouraged to upgrade to patched versions or disable HTTP/2 functionality.

infosec.title: Hundreds of Websites Deliver Potent Malware Cocktail to Unsuspecting Visitors
infosec.summary: Attackers modified JavaScript served through Optimizely's legitimate infrastructure, affecting 178 sites, including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce. The malicious track.js script replaced cryptocurrency wallet addresses, captured card numbers, CVVs, cookies, and screenshots, and served Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits. ReportURI says funds were stolen from some visitors. Optimizely has not explained how attackers gained write access.

infosec.title: Backdooring LLMs - Do You Trust Your AI Provider?
infosec.summary: Paolo Galeone fine-tuned Qwen3-8B with a QLoRA adapter on one RTX 3090, for about €1 of electricity, so that a harmless question about 23 May 1992 made it silently emit a bash tool call that the pi agent harness executed with an empty visible reply. By training on pi's actual system prompt, he made the backdoor fire only in pi, making it dormant in other harnesses like Claude Code and Codex. A merged adapter shows up when you diff weights against the official base, since layernorm weights stay unchanged, but that doesn't work for hosted API models, so defenders should sandbox agents, require approval for shell and network tool calls, and test new models with their real harness prompt.

infosec.title: Abusing the Windows Smart Card Minidriver Architecture
infosec.summary: A low-privileged user can run malware that uses a victim's plugged-in smart card remotely, because Windows lets any process load the card's minidriver and call CardAuthenticateEx() and CardSignData() directly. The researcher's proxy, called Hermes, hooks CardAuthenticateEx() to capture the PIN, then signs attacker-supplied data over an SMB named pipe that an emulated card connects to through a modified OpenSC minidriver, and this works with any card type or algorithm. The behavior is by design and not a vulnerability, so defenders should watch for unexpected processes loading smart card minidrivers or hooking their exports, and should not treat smart card authentication alone as proof that the user is physically present.

infosec.title: Pass-the-Device
infosec.summary: Pass-the-Device is the companion toolkit to a CODE BLUE 2026 talk on carrying SASE and VPN device trust off a compromised endpoint. It pairs red team recon tools for GlobalProtect, Cisco ASA, FortiGate, Zscaler, and Netskope with Sigma and KQL detections for blue teams. The recon side fingerprints VPN auth methods and IdPs, enumerates Netskope tenant configuration anonymously, parses Cisco HostScan posture profiles, and includes a lab SAML proxy that injects PRT cookies. The detections flag non-vendor processes reading VPN client state or DPAPI master keys, along with the default fingerprints of OpenConnect-based clients, and defenders should baseline them before alerting on them.

A public-only token with write:admin, issued by a site admin, could list private organizations and user emails, create a user, promote it to site admin, and mint Actions runner registration tokens.

infosec.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
infosec.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731, a CVSS 9.4 deserialization flaw in Perforce Puppet's report processing, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. A client with a CA-signed agent certificate can submit crafted rich-data in a PUT request and run code as the Puppet Server service user. Weak automatic certificate signing can expose unauthenticated attackers. RCE may expose CA signing keys, enable host impersonation, ransomware, data theft, and lateral movement. Perforce patched affected Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Core versions on November 3. OpenVox also issued fixes.

Database roles remain the final guardrail. The takeaway: authorize the query's actual dependencies, not just its visible output.

data.title: Reduce Your Data Pipelines, One Database, Every Data Type
data.summary: Oracle AI Database combines relational, JSON, graph, and vector data in one engine, reducing the need to copy data into separate systems. Try it free on Oracle LiveLabs.

data.title: Rethinking Table File Paths with Uber: Lance's Multi-Base Layout
data.summary: Lance's multi-base layout lets one dataset span multiple storage locations, improving portability and avoiding rewrite-heavy path migrations as data scales across buckets.

data.title: Data work is coding now
data.summary: AI is making it easier for anyone to analyze data and build apps by generating the code for them.

design.title: How .raw reworked STOW's identity to make its coffee roasting visible
design.summary: Slovenian branding studio .raw has redesigned specialty coffee company STOW's identity to communicate the scientific precision behind its sourcing, roasting, and testing processes. The system retains STOW's original factory-inspired symbol while introducing a geometric wordmark, Aeonik Mono typography, structured layouts, and square brackets borrowed from scientific notation. A restrained black, white, and gray palette is complemented by five accent colors representing different flavor profiles, making the brand's technical expertise and sensory qualities visible across packaging, menus, and other applications.

design.title: Google tests sticky citations in desktop AI Overviews
design.summary: Google is testing a new desktop AI Overview interface that keeps source citations visible as users scroll through AI-generated answers. The citations move with the content instead of disappearing offscreen, making it easier to access supporting websites while reading longer responses. The experiment also introduces a horizontal divider separating the AI Overview from conventional search results, and the design has been spotted across multiple browsers.

design.title: Spotify's New Tool Aims to Stop Deepfakes from Being Attributed to Real Artists
design.summary: Spotify is rolling out Artist Profile Protection to all artists, letting them review and remove releases submitted under their name after an eight-month beta. Artists get alerts when new music appears under their name, and an advanced setting holds releases until they manually approve them. The launch follows Billboard's report that Sony Music sought removal of more than 260,000 deepfake songs from digital platforms.

design.title: AI is the New Old Design Material
design.summary: Designers have always learned their medium by working it, and AI models are the next material. A mockup shows one sample, while a model returns a distribution of answers that only sampling code reveals. Running each prompt 50 times, bringing the worst answers to design review, and saving failures as shared test cases puts that spread in front of the team.

design.title: Your path to design engineering
design.summary: Design engineering combines the ability to solve design problems with responsibility for implementing those solutions, but the skills needed depend on whether someone comes from design, frontend engineering, or a different background. Frontend engineers can develop design judgment by exploring alternative layouts and understanding visual hierarchy, while designers can learn to translate their decisions into functional interfaces and handle real-world implementation constraints. This choose-your-own-adventure learning guide offers practical exercises for each starting point, emphasizing small projects, iterative practice, and understanding the reasoning behind design and engineering decisions.

design.title: AI Sped up the Build: How Can Accessibility Testing Keep Up?
design.summary: AI has sped up planning, design, and development, but only 30% of professionals in Level Access' survey of 2,500+ report gains in QA and testing. WebAIM found detected errors per home page rose 10.1%, while organizations that keep improving use AI at the same rate but invest more in training and culture. Accessibility judgment moves earlier through annotated handoffs, gated pull requests, and AI-drafted fixes reviewed in context, each leaving a regression test behind.

design.title: Rare Animated React Components
design.summary: Rare UI is a free, open-source collection of rare animated React components.

design.title: React Loaders for Generative UI
design.summary: Animated React loaders for text, inline, and image generation states.

design.title: Free, Installable Design Systems for Agents
design.summary: Free design systems for AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor.

design.title: Design Engineering Has a Handoff Problem
design.summary: AI-generated components from designers were meant to lighten engineers' load, but ones with hardcoded values and inline SVGs now pile up in engineers' review queues. The handoff has simply moved down a level, with designers lacking the governance, permissions, and shared tooling engineering built over years. The fix starts with holding designer code to the same merge bar, running deterministic checks before human review, and giving designers a lighter environment.

design.title: Prevent UX Theater with Cross-Functional Collaboration
design.summary: UX theater occurs when organizations perform design activities without meaningfully involving users or allowing research to influence decisions. Cross-functional collaboration can help counter this by bringing designers, researchers, developers, and other stakeholders into shared discussions about user needs and product priorities. Meaningful collaboration requires teams to move beyond workshops and deliverables toward evidence-based decisions, shared accountability, and genuine participation in the design process.

design.title: AI's Role in the Creative Process
design.summary: Debates pitting AI enthusiasts against skeptics miss the real question: which parts of creative work to automate and which to keep. Tedious labor like VFX green-screen cleanup can go, but friction such as trimming a shot or drafting a brief is where thinking happens. Figma's Gaussian splat campaign, generated with Seedance 2.5 in Weave, still took long rounds of riffing before its shots felt finished.

design.title: Disney's Radical New Animation Technique Will Make Hexed the End of an Era
design.summary: Hexed may be the last original Disney film in the studio's familiar 3D style, as every original from Clay onward gets its own look.

design.title: Artists and creators are leaving Etsy in droves over its new AI policy
design.summary: Artists and independent sellers are closing their Etsy stores after forthcoming terms explicitly authorize the platform and its partners to use seller content for AI training, testing, and development, despite Etsy's assurances that it does not train models to copy or replace creators' work.

design.title: How to experiment when designing in a regulated field like Healthcare UX
design.summary: Rapid experimentation is increasingly accessible through AI tools, but designers working in healthcare and finance face strict regulations around sensitive data, privacy, and product safety.

marketing.title: Atlassian's AI Marketing Playbook for Campaigns, Creative Production & Reporting
marketing.summary: AI can draft a brief and content in minutes. But campaigns still take weeks to launch, creative gets trapped in revision cycles, and reporting takes hours to pull together. Atlassian's AI Marketing Playbook is a practical guide to making AI deliver for marketing, where you'll learn how to: Build stronger campaign plans, move into execution faster, and maintain momentum as priorities change. Increase creative capacity while protecting time for ideas, craft, and quality. Move from performance signals to decisions and action sooner. You'll also get a practical framework for choosing a high-value workflow to transform, piloting it on real work, and measuring the impact. Get the playbook.

marketing.title: Marketers to Spend $116 Billion on Creators in 2026
marketing.summary: Brand spending on creators is forecast to grow 15% in 2026 and reach $178 billion by 2030, about twice the pace of advertising. Paid amplification of creator content makes up 44% of spending, while paying creators for content rather than reach is the fastest-growing segment. Most of the growth comes from budgets shifted out of TV, performance media, and creative production rather than new marketing dollars.

marketing.title: 94% of global hits went viral on TikTok first, reveals 2026 Music Impact Report
marketing.summary: TikTok has become a major driver of music discovery and commercial success. 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on the platform first. Songs that go viral on TikTok spend four times longer on the chart than non-viral tracks, and 45% of US TikTok users discover new music on the platform. That discovery also translates into purchases: TikTok music listeners are 78% more likely to pay for a streaming subscription, and 61% purchased physical or digital music in the past year.

marketing.title: Win Report: How cutting overwhelm grew conversions by 13%
marketing.summary: Reducing the effort required to compare options can increase conversions, especially when a page overwhelms visitors with too much information. Churnet Valley Railway replaced its long list of eight dining experiences with categorized sections that put popular options first and compact cards that made prices, departure times, and durations easy to compare. It also replaced the “Book Now” CTA with “Check Running Times” to give visitors a lower-commitment next step into the booking process. The redesign increased conversions by 13%, with an even stronger result among first-time visitors.

marketing.title: 5 ways to personalize your emails, from a study of 274 billion sends
marketing.summary: Personalize emails by referencing shoppers' recent activity, such as products they browsed, items in their cart, or their last purchase. Use signup preferences to tailor welcome emails, and include product-specific care tips, how-to content, or complementary product recommendations in post-purchase emails. Show/hide logic can also display different content to different segments in a single campaign, such as VIP offers for loyalty members or location-specific promotions. Klaviyo's analysis of 274 billion emails found that messages that referenced shoppers' recent activity earned 45% higher click rates in flows and 33% higher click rates in campaigns.

marketing.title: 5 tips to increasing LinkedIn video reach
marketing.summary: With LinkedIn reach declining, prioritize timely topics tied to current conversations and use on-screen text hooks that create curiosity rather than simply describe the video. Keep footage clear and audio crisp without overcomplicating production. Focus on content that offers value viewers can apply or save. Listicles and self-improvement formats are gaining traction. Avoid excessive transitions and visual effects that distract from the message.

marketing.title: What's Next for AI Search in 2027 with Kevin Indig and Eli Schwartz
marketing.summary: Should you be writing 10x more blog posts? Chasing citations on Reddit? Or a different strategy altogether? On December 8 , AI search exports Kevin Indig and Eli Schwartz will dive into the data, the myths - and three bets on where to invest next. Register now

marketing.title: The AI Ad Creative Masterclass: Skills, Tools, and the 21 Formats Top Brands Run
marketing.summary: 24 of the 34 longest-running Meta ads from 48 top DTC brands were simple stills. Creator videos were the most tested video format but among the first switched off, with a median run of 38 days. Strong batches mix at least 4 formats and 3 buying angles, with stills built to run for months and videos replaced every few weeks.

marketing.title: WriteStack
marketing.summary: WriteStack is a Substack growth platform that helps creators turn Notes into free and paid subscribers. Its AI Coach generates Notes and outlines in the creator's voice and helps edit articles. Creators can batch schedule Notes and use analytics to see which posts drive subscriptions. The platform also streamlines notifications and supports cross-posting to other social channels, and AI agent integrations.

marketing.title: 3 things I'm watching in marketing going into 2027
marketing.summary: Brands are replacing some agency work with in-house creators and employee advocates to build trust through individual voices. Engaged communities are becoming more valuable than large follower counts as brands seek direct audience relationships beyond algorithm-dependent platforms. Meanwhile, audiences are tuning out generic claims of authenticity. Original perspectives and behind-the-scenes content are becoming more effective ways to stand out.

marketing.title: Why you WANT more unsubscribes
marketing.summary: A very low unsubscribe rate can mean email is landing in spam, since nobody unsubscribes from a junk folder. Unsubscribing is also the least damaging way to leave, since a spam report hurts placement and silent non-readers drag it down over time. Splitting unsubscribes by opt-in type separates intentional sign-ups, whose exits signal a content problem, from consequential ones like gated downloads, whose quick exits are expected. Making the exit easy, and occasionally inviting it, keeps people who are done from reaching for the spam button.

marketing.title: AI product recommendations are mostly a summary of listicles
marketing.summary: A study across 4 search engines found that 90% of recommended brands appeared on at least one cited “best X” or “top X” list. Brands featured on 3 or more cited lists were recommended 44% of the time, compared with just 2.5% for brands absent from all lists. The top 10 list publishers accounted for up to 90% of citations in some categories. Updated comparisons also mattered, with 83% of Gemini's cited pages featuring 2026 in the title or URL.

marketing.title: When Did ‘Grand Theft Auto' Become Brand Safe?
marketing.summary: GTA is no longer an automatic brand safety risk, but brands must weigh its cultural relevance against whether its provocative world fits their identity and audience.

marketing.title: Google Is Making More Room for News in AI Search
marketing.summary: Sites like Reddit report receiving less traffic from Google despite frequent appearances in AI answers.

founders.title: Give your sales pipeline to an AI employee
founders.summary: Viktor is an AI employee in Slack, Microsoft Teams and email. Give him the pipeline. Every weekday at 8:30 he reads each open deal in HubSpot, Attio or Pipedrive, with its emails, call notes and Slack mentions: • Flags deals that went quiet• Spots trials ending this week• Drafts each follow-up in your voice Nothing goes out until the owner approves, and then he updates the deal stage in the CRM. On Fridays he posts what moved, what stalled and the 5 deals worth a push. Use code TLDR at viktor.com/tldr for 20,000 bonus credits (new workspaces, until January 31).

founders.title: Why are all the indie-friendly products dying at the same time?
founders.summary: More venture-backed startups have shut down this year than in any year on record. Many of these companies were founded or fundraised when raising capital was easy, and couldn't fundraise again this year. The companies that are surviving tend to be bootstrapped, profitable tools that don't need venture capital, local-first software where people can self-host or 'bring your own cloud', and API-first platforms that can be used as a primitive for custom things.

founders.title: State of Pre-Seed: Q3 2026
founders.summary: A SAFE puts off pricing a startup, but its valuation cap can already decide what the investor pays. Carta's latest US data shows most SAFEs converted at their cap among companies that went on to raise a seed round. Seed valuations usually land above the cap, so negotiate the cap as the likely price. Median caps rose across every round size while total pre-seed dollars grew and the number of deals fell.

founders.title: How Fast Do You Really Have to Be Growing to Raise Venture Capital Today? $1M to $100M ARR in 5 Years, Max. But VCs Are Hoping for 2-3 Years
founders.summary: A software company can beat median growth and still struggle to raise venture money. SaaStr's proposed benchmark is reaching $100 million in annual recurring revenue within five years of hitting $1 million. Lower public-market revenue multiples mean a company needs more revenue to reach the same exit value, so investors push that requirement back to earlier rounds. Strong retention and large infrastructure contracts can earn a company more time under the framework. Private equity and growth equity remain options for slower growers.

founders.title: A Primer on AI-Enabled Roll-Ups
founders.summary: Selling software to service firms leaves most of the money in those industries out of reach. US spending on accounting services is about 34 times spending on accounting software. AI-enabled roll-ups go after that bigger budget by buying existing firms and running them on their own AI tools. The primer recommends using the gains to serve more clients with the same staff. Its industry screen favors fragmented markets with cheap acquisition prices and more demand than firms can staff.

founders.title: The B2B buyer journey with AI
founders.summary: Buyers increasingly ask ChatGPT or Claude which software to buy before they visit a vendor's site. Growth Unhinged studied about 27,000 buying prompts to see what those buyers wanted to know. Most prompts compared specific products, while only 15% involved early research. Pricing was the biggest single topic, including early questions about coding agents and website builders. Check what AI tools say about your prices and features, since a wrong answer can drop you from the shortlist.

founders.title: The Observability Engineering Masterclass
founders.summary: As distributed systems grow more complex, effective observability becomes increasingly important. This six-part masterclass with engineering leader Liz Fong-Jones explores technical practices that help teams understand system behavior and improve reliability. Learn from the expert and explore actionable approaches. Get the free masterclass.

founders.title: AWS launches credit splitting and transfers
founders.summary: AWS now lets customers divide a credit and transfer portions to linked accounts under the same payer account, so startup credits can go to the team that earned them. Splits are permanent and keep the original expiration date at no extra cost.

founders.title: Security risk assessments run automatically on GitHub Team
founders.summary: GitHub now runs free security risk assessments automatically for organizations on the GitHub Team plan. Admins can review exposed credentials and code vulnerabilities in one place to decide what to fix first.

founders.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
founders.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join .

founders.title: Introducing Vercel X
founders.summary: Vercel X is a six-week accelerator for AI founders in the idea and pre-seed stages. The cohort of 40 teams will build alongside Vercel's product leaders, designers, and engineers. The program will take no equity for participation, and there is a program-wide pool of more than $9 million in credits from Vercel, AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI, and other partners. Applications are open until November 29, and the program will run from January 19 to March 2.

founders.title: B2B PR That Gets Results with Michelle Garrett
founders.summary: Michelle Garrett discusses effective B2B PR strategies, emphasizing the importance of targeted media lists and ongoing engagement over sporadic press releases. She highlights how building relationships with trade editors and focusing on specific industry publications can yield better results than a broad "spray and pray" approach. Garrett also advises incorporating visuals in PR content and tailoring case studies to address multiple stakeholders within B2B decision-making processes.

founders.title: There is only one company to build
founders.summary: There's a single shape/direction emerging across all of the players in enterprise AI. Every company across the training data supply chain is becoming an AI transformation business. The only thing enterprise actually wants to buy is a change in their business. Founders can charge a lot more and have an easier time selling this if they just say they will sell the change enterprises want to make.

founders.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
founders.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach founders, operators and startup leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

founders.title: An AI Agent Is Not Your Next Customer
founders.summary: Almost nobody is using agents for transactions, and it's not a technical issue.

founders.title: Contexting vs. Context
founders.summary: One product leader blamed their team for vague questions, then caught themselves doing the same to their own boss.

founders.title: Their Highest-Revenue Email Looked Like a Personal Note
founders.summary: An email resembling a personal note generated the highest revenue for an ecommerce company, suggesting presentation trumps the offer itself.

founders.title: Google Ads AI Max Is Making More Decisions For You – Here's What To Audit Now
founders.summary: Google Ads is giving automation a larger role in how ads are matched, written, and delivered.

crypto.title: Anthropic IPO: how do traders get 2x the move?
crypto.summary: Anthropic is going public, and GraniteShares is launching two 2x ETFs on it. AIL → bullish, seeks 2x Anthropic's daily move ANS → bearish, seeks 2x the opposite Anthropic +1% → AIL seeks +2% Anthropic −1% → ANS seeks +2% Built for traders who want to act on a short-term view of Anthropic, up or down, in one ticker, no margin needed. Coming soon to your trading apps. Learn about AIL and ANS

crypto.title: Coinbase Launches Official ChatGPT Plugin for Agentic Trading
crypto.summary: Coinbase has launched a ChatGPT plugin that lets users connect their Coinbase account to trade stocks, crypto, and derivatives without leaving the chat interface. Users retain approval authority over each order, keeping execution within the existing conversation flow. This is the first app in the ChatGPT plugin store that enables financial transactions.

crypto.title: Solana Foundation Acquires Majority Stake in CoinGecko
crypto.summary: The Solana Foundation acquired a majority stake in CoinGecko, the leading crypto data platform founded in Malaysia in 2014 by Bobby Ong and TM Lee, which serves tens of millions of monthly users and 180,000 developers and businesses with pricing and market data. Post-acquisition plans include integrating Solana-native trading and DeFi experiences directly into the platform and expanding CoinGecko's coverage to equities and real-world assets. The deal gives Solana direct distribution to CoinGecko's developer and API base, positioning the chain as the primary DeFi execution layer for the platform's next product phase.

crypto.title: Coinflow Spend: settle instantly, spend anywhere, earn 2% cash back
crypto.summary: Coinflow Spend allows merchant revenue to settle into a Coinflow balance in seconds, 24/7. Merchants can issue virtual cards to employees with individual limits, topped up from that balance. The cards work anywhere Visa is accepted. Transactions are exportable for accounting. Qualified spending will earn uncapped 2% cash back until March 31.

crypto.title: Street: Board-Aligned Private Equity Secondary Marketplace
crypto.summary: Street launched out of stealth as a board-aligned private equity secondary marketplace, disclosing $200M in open interest on day one. CEO Lukas Gruber cited OpenAI and Anthropic's public disclosures that billions in their secondary sales were illicit and voided, and that 5 of 6 major secondary platforms had closed transactions without board knowledge, as the catalyst for building a compliant alternative. Street has partnered with Google and established capital allocators to deliver a brokerage-style experience rather than a traditional secondary marketplace. The company's stated long-term goal is to become the American Exchange for Private Equity, competing with SPV-based structures that have dominated private secondary markets.

crypto.title: How tokenized deposits actually settle
crypto.summary: Tokenized deposits like Citi Token Services and JPMorgan's Kinexys are “on-us,” staying within one bank's legal entity. Moving them between banks requires interbank settlement, since the receiving bank otherwise holds an unsecured claim on the sender. Swift's Shared Ledger locks the deposit and lets the receiving bank credit immediately, but settlement is deferred through RTGS, leaving credit exposure in between. Issuing a tokenized deposit on an internal ledger is necessary but not sufficient for better interbank settlement.

crypto.title: Beyond the Bot: Mapping the Agentic Trading Stack
crypto.summary: The agentic trading space can be mapped into four layers: Intelligence (data and market reasoning models), Agency (harnesses, terminals, and copilots), Execution (venue connectivity), and Compliance and Observability (trust infrastructure for autonomous decisions). In the Agency layer, OpenClaw accumulated ~250K GitHub stars in 60 days, with trading-specialized harnesses like Senpi and Supertake and cross-asset terminals such as Catalyst competing across stocks, options, and prediction markets. The agent itself carries no moat, since open-source models on open-source harnesses commoditize agent capability, placing value with whoever owns the decision loop (Intent-as-a-Service), platforms with the deepest liquidity, and custodians trusted across the broadest asset class range. Coinbase Ventures is investing across three pillars: harnesses and terminals that deliver portfolio-building intent, proprietary intelligence and specialized market reasoning models, and compliance/observability infrastructure covering agent identity and tamper-proof decision logs.

crypto.title: ChatGPT Wallet is the right bet on the wrong timeline
crypto.summary: OpenAI chose network agentic tokens, the right long-term approach, but incentives aren't aligned yet. Users get a worse experience (credit cards only, Face ID on every purchase, and thin recurring support). Merchants still carry dispute risk with no network liability framework, and one in three of 174 top stores couldn't reach guest checkout in one test. Issuers approve blind, with no standard view of intent and no answer on who absorbs chargebacks, and Visa expects agentic commerce to stay small through FY2027. OpenAI isn't taking a cut yet and lacks an Apple Pay-style deal. One should expect a fallback to raw card details in the near term.

crypto.title: If I were building a neobank today
crypto.summary: The post communicates 30 principles for a new neobank. Chief among them: go B2B for $50M+ revenue businesses in boring, cash-rich niches, with distribution as the only moat, credit products and underwriting as defensibility, and lending your own capital for higher margins. Dominate one industry first, choose the sponsor bank carefully, support stablecoins from day one, obsess over onboarding speed and compliance, and avoid competing on cashback alone. The biggest competitor is JPMorgan, and it's not worth calling yourself a neobank.

crypto.title: Former UK PM Mangles Satoshi's Name on Camera
crypto.summary: Former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson repeatedly mangled Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto's pseudonym on camera, referring to him as "Yakko-Mucko Nakasako" and "Yakamoto Nakasori" while conceding that nobody knows who controls Bitcoin.

crypto.title: Tether Capital invests in Stables to expand USDT payments
crypto.summary: Tether Capital made a strategic investment, with no amount disclosed, in Stables, which offers a single API connecting local banking systems to USDT settlement across more than 160 markets and over $2B in annual USDT volume.

crypto.title: On-chain derivatives are now 58% crypto and 42% RWA
crypto.summary: Markets keep falling, but the shift inside is accelerating.

crypto.summary: Subscriptions for tokenized Anthropic shares run 06:00 to 14:00 UTC on November 18 in USDC.

fintech.title: Tech work driven by bold ideas. Backed by institutional scale.
fintech.summary: You don't have to choose between cutting-edge development and stability. At Fidelity, you'll have the opportunity to pursue your curiosity, create impactful technology, and grow your career: ● Meaningful work: Tools that empower everyday people to navigate their financial lives ● Time to build: Dedicated hours to explore emerging tech , test approaches, and sharpen your craft ● Encouragement to grow: A career-focused culture with dedicated upskilling time Bring your experience to a place that's looking to the future. Discover technology careers at Fidelity and find a fit for your skills. Fidelity is an equal opportunity employer.

fintech.title: Klarna taps Robinhood VP Chris Koegel as CFO
fintech.summary: Klarna has appointed Chris Koegel as its new chief financial officer starting in January. Koegel served as vice president, head of corporate finance, and investor relations at cryptocurrency platform Robinhood. He joined the company in 2022 and saw its valuation grow from under $10 billion to over $100 billion.

fintech.title: PayPal partners with Workday to enhance employee financial wellbeing
fintech.summary: PayPal announced a partnership with Workday that lets employees of Workday customers set up PayPal Direct Deposit through Workday's Enhanced Direct Deposit (EDD) program, giving eligible employees in the US a way to receive their pay up to two days early.

fintech.title: The last mile problem for stablecoins
fintech.summary: Stablecoins let small banks transact directly across borders, but the final leg into local currency still carries FX, compliance, and funding costs. Mastercard's BVNK-powered Global Money Platform is the center that absorbs them.

fintech.title: Should Tesla and SpaceX merge?
fintech.summary: Mostly Metrics weighs the industrial logic of combining Tesla and SpaceX against the risk of creating a sprawling conglomerate that investors may value less clearly. A merger could simplify shared projects such as Terafab, improve capital and talent allocation, and vertically integrate chips, energy, satellites, AI, and robotics, but the companies have very different growth rates, margins, and capital needs, and many of the operational benefits could potentially be achieved through partnerships instead.

fintech.title: Can Revolut dominate the US without taking risk?
fintech.summary: Revolut's US bank will be credit-card led. It will match Amex and Chase perks while keeping lending under 10% of the balance sheet and securitizing the rest. Chase earned about $23.8 billion in card net interest income in 2025 versus $2.2 billion in net non-interest card revenue. Perks are acquisition costs and the loan is the product, so Revolut must choose between dominating and taking little risk.

fintech.title: Block's turnaround strategy: two ecosystems, one bank
fintech.summary: Block's turnaround came from narrowing its focus, cutting more than 40% of staff, consolidating around Square and Cash App, and then using its bank charter to scale consumer lending. Cash App now drives most of Block's growth, with $19 billion of quarterly consumer lending originations and rising gross profit per user, while Square is re-accelerating through stronger distribution, but the strategy also concentrates more risk in credit losses and regulatory controls.

fintech.title: Life after the Swipe
fintech.summary: This post walks through what happens after a card swipe and how card programs are built. Stablecoin-linked cards let issuers launch in 10 to 30+ markets from one dollar-denominated sponsor like Rain instead of a bank partner per country. Visa and Mastercard now accept stablecoin settlement seven days a week, so a multi-market program can collapse separate prefunded pots into one balance. Issuers also get new features: yield on dollar balances, loyalty rewards at any merchant terminal, and global co-brand cards for fan bases. Large domestic banks gain little from “T-shaped” programs (wide across markets and deep in products) like this.

fintech.title: Cards work best when they plug into workflows customers already use
fintech.summary: See how fintechs, platforms, and consumer brands are building card programs powered by customer data . Download the guide →

fintech.title: Mastercard opens Singapore innovation centre of excellence
fintech.summary: Mastercard has opened an innovation centre of excellence in Singapore that will eventually house 250 specialists working in areas such as AI, digital commerce, and cybersecurity.

fintech.title: Plaid launches Agent Detection to identify AI-driven financial activity
fintech.summary: Plaid launched Agent Detection to help banks and fintechs distinguish human activity from AI agents across login, onboarding, account linking, and money movement, including identifying which AI provider is behind a session. Plaid says the system detected 2.3x more agent sessions than competitors in live testing, and views it as the first layer of broader infrastructure for trusted agentic finance, where institutions can recognize agents, assess risk, and eventually let consumers authorize specific actions safely.

fintech.title: Anthropic IPO could deliver huge gains for early investors
fintech.summary: Anthropic's expected IPO at a valuation of at least $1.33 trillion could generate major gains for a broad investor base spanning venture firms, large technology companies, private equity, and sovereign wealth funds. The company most recently raised private capital at a $965 billion valuation, meaning the IPO could mark another substantial step-up for existing shareholders.

fintech.title: Blue J lands $176m to put AI agents on tax desks
fintech.summary: Blue J raised a $176 million Series E led by JMI Equity at a valuation above $700 million to expand Workflows, an agentic product that checks returns before filing, drafts replies to IRS notices, and reviews partnership agreements. The company says ARR grew 165% in the 15 months after its Series D, and that more than 6,500 organizations use its research engine.

fintech.title: Banks risk losing the customer relationship as AI becomes the financial interface
fintech.summary: Banks and credit unions risk becoming passive data providers if consumers increasingly turn to AI assistants for financial guidance.

fintech.title: Italian court places Revolut unit under supervision over anti-money laundering failures
fintech.summary: An Italian court placed Revolut Bank UAB's Italian operations under one year of judicial administration after finding serious anti-money laundering deficiencies that allegedly allowed 24 suspected or convicted criminals to move €41.9 million through the bank without Revolut filing any suspicious transaction reports.

it.title: You can't AI-wash your way to trust
it.summary: AI copilots are fine for individuals. But when you're dealing with sensitive IP and complex legacy systems for an enterprise? Not so much. There is an alternative - and it's trusted by 50% of the Fortune 50. Redwood RangerAI was specifically trained for service orchestration and workload automation use cases. Enterprise workflows are part of its wiring, not a prompt. Use it to: Accelerate development and reduce risk by generating automation scripts and documentation Pass task-specific data that remains private, governed and auditable Get comprehensive, real-time visibility into workflows Produce predictive SLA monitoring and intel dashboards for optimization, compliance and automatic self-recovery Meet RangerAI

it.title: AWS announces general availability of AWS Interconnect
it.summary: AWS Interconnect now links AWS and Microsoft Azure privately, replacing the do-it-yourself networking customers previously had to build.

it.title: Microsoft and organizations across industries launch AI Transparency Initiative to strengthen enterprise trust in AI models and agents
it.summary: The initiative aims to establish open, industrywide standards for AI security, governance, and transparency across models and providers to help enterprises independently verify AI agent behavior.

it.title: AI is blurring the lines between CIO, CISO, and CRO
it.summary: Autonomous agentic AI in enterprise environments blurs traditional organizational lines between the CIO, CISO, and CRO because current governance models rely on human decision structures that are too slow. As agents make rapid operational decisions with broad consequences, organizations lack clear definitions of operational authority and risk ownership. Companies need to establish explicit decision mandates, pre-agreed tie-breaks, and comprehensive decision trails to maintain human accountability.

it.title: A bottle-cap manufacturer offers a reality check on AI
it.summary: A manufacturer's presentation challenged the assumption that every business process is ready for AI automation, pointing to aging equipment, limited digital skills, and thin margins. Successful adoption starts with understanding employees' practical knowledge and operational constraints.

it.title: Even the best AI model doesn't know your business
it.summary: Your workflows, approvals, and exceptions aren't built into any model. In this Dataiku-sponsored article , Rush Deshpande explains how to build AI around your business, with people, orchestration, and governance at the center, even as models change. Read more here.

it.title: Put Gemini to work for you
it.summary: Gemini Tasks can perform agentic actions such as calling businesses, booking appointments, managing calendars, and completing purchases via Google Pay. The assistant integrates with Google apps like Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive, and Calendar to handle multi-step projects and routine busywork. The new features are powered by Google's latest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.

it.title: Windows security at Ignite 2026: Start secure, protect what matters, prepare for AI
it.summary: Microsoft has announced general availability of its Windows endpoint security platform, which gives third-party security vendors a way to protect systems without relying as heavily on kernel-level software. Developers can use the new API to warn users, limit functionality, or block applications from running if a PC fails the security check.

it.title: Enterprise Deployment of Governed Agents on Windows
it.summary: Windows and Microsoft tools are working together to support enterprise deployment of governed AI agents through identity, containment, and management primitives. Microsoft Entra Agent ID and Microsoft Execution Containers provide platform-enforced boundaries, while Microsoft Intune, Defender, and Purview extend management, runtime protection, and data loss prevention to local agent workloads.

it.title: Java4Shell flaw exposes widely used enterprise applications
it.summary: Oracle patched a Java vulnerability that can let unauthenticated attackers execute code or crash affected systems. Researchers demonstrated attacks against applications including Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and Elasticsearch, with exposure depending on the underlying Java version and CPU configuration.

it.title: Intel secures expanded Azure infrastructure partnership
it.summary: Microsoft's expanded Intel agreement includes multi-year Xeon supply and plans to use Intel's EMIB packaging technology for Azure's own chips.

it.title: The knowledge layer for enterprise AI: Domain Ontology
it.summary: A Neo4j-based ontology helps enterprise AI agents interpret ambiguous business terms using governed definitions, rules, and provenance.
